text:
Jordan R: evening takeover :wave: quick pass — summary of the P2 alert that fired earlier.
Jordan R: TL;DR: routing-service saw a sudden 5xx spike at ~19:12 UTC, primarily impacting EU-W. We routed traffic away, scaled the unhappy pool, and rolled a small config tweak. No degraded SLA so far, but customer-facing latency did spike for ~8m.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER sev2 — routing-service: elevated 5xx rate (19:12 UTC). Pager link: https://pager.example/incident/2384
Samira V: saw the pager. Which pods were throwing 5xx? stack traces?
Jordan R: most errors were 502/504 from the routing proxy -> worker timeouts. Logs show `kv-cache` RPC timeouts and `dispatch` queue backpressure. Not a model OOM.
Lee C: confirmed — stack traces point to `dispatch` goroutine backlog. Metric: dispatch_queue_length spiked to 1200 (baseline ~50). p95 token latency up x4.
Maya P: any customer hits? Did any keys fail authentication or was it pure latency/timeout?
Jordan R: primary customer impact was elevated latency and some requests returning 502. Auth OK. Affected subset was EU-W routing path.
Lee C: mitigation we did:
- increased routing-service replicas from 6 -> 12 (k8s horizontal scale)
- enabled fallback-route for EU-W to route to eu-central for low-priority traffic
- restarted the most-recently deployed worker pod group (deployment/worker-eu-w) as a conservative step

Commands used:
```
kubectl -n runtime scale deploy/routing-service --replicas=12
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deploy/worker-eu-w
```
Jordan R: also temporarily increased dispatch worker concurrency via config flag `dispatch.max_workers=150` to relieve queue.
Samira V: good. Do we know root cause yet? rollout-induced or load surge?
Lee C: preliminary looks like a combination: a small load burst (third-party crawler hitting embed endpoints) + an under‑provisioned dispatch queue after yesterday's config change that lowered max_workers.
Maya P: any ongoing backlog or pages?
Jordan R: no new pages since ~19:24 UTC. last few minutes: errors within normal noise. dispatch_queue_length back to ~40. p95 still slightly elevated but trending down.
incident-bot: Incident 2384 now marked: mitigated (19:29 UTC) — monitoring for regressions.
Samira V: runbook pointers for follow-up?
opsbot: Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/runbooks/routing-service-5xx. Play sections: "evict-backpressured-workers", "enable-fallback-route", "scale-routing-service".
Lee C: noted follow-ups for tomorrow:
- revert the temporary `dispatch.max_workers` increase if not needed
- add a short-term rate-limiter for the crawler signature seen in logs (IP CIDR / user-agent)
- add an alert to catch dispatch_queue_length > 500 earlier
Jordan R: coverage note for the rest of my shift (00:00 UTC handoff):
- primary: Jordan R (me) until 00:00 UTC
- secondary: Samira V (on pager) until 02:00 UTC
- backup: Lee C
Samira V: I'll take secondary — able to respond to pages through 02:00 UTC. If anything looks like a rollout regression, ping infra-dev for emergency rollback.
Maya P: any customer comms needed?
Jordan R: engineering blip only; CS flagged one enterprise tenant with raised latency. Maya, please coordinate a short note: "observed elevated latency for a small subset of requests in EU-W; mitigation applied; no data loss; currently stable." Keep it light unless they request more.
Maya P: will draft and post in #customer-notifications, link back here.
Samira V: outstanding action items (short):
- Lee: add alert for dispatch_queue_length > 500 (P3) — ETA 1h
- Jordan: create a follow-up ticket to rate-limit crawler UA and schedule review with infra (ETA EOD)
- Maya: customer note (ASAP)
Jordan R: handoff checklist complete for now. If anything spikes, page the SEV channel and @Samira V. Logging snippets and grep patterns used earlier in thread.
Lee C: quick note — I captured `kubectl describe` + container logs to the incident artifact: s3://incidents/2384/logs.tar.gz
Jordan R: thanks team — leaving my pager on low-sound for an hour but reachable. :thumbsup:
Samira V: acknowledged. Good luck, enjoy the rest of the evening.
incident-bot: Incident 2384 closed (19:44 UTC) — monitoring window open for 2h.
Jordan R: last update — no regressions over 30m. handing over tidy state to night shift.
